blockdesc-machine-gather-*: Awakened sparkstone carved with the Gather glyph. Each aligned crystal in its sockets gathers charge from its alignment's surroundings straight into the network.
blockdesc-machine-refine-*: Awakened sparkstone carved with the Refine glyph. Its aligned crystal is a pattern: Unaligned crystals beside it, of its Evolution or lower, take its alignment in a day or two, for charge.
blockdesc-machine-focus-*: Awakened sparkstone carved with the Focus glyph. Each crystal in its sockets works its own evocation, in turn, on what its front looks at, for a tenth of a cast's charge.
blockdesc-machine-scatter-*: Awakened sparkstone carved with the Scatter glyph. Like a Focus, one Evolution weaker, across a flat square nine blocks by nine.
blockdesc-machine-amplify-*: Awakened sparkstone carved with the Amplify glyph. It lifts the Focus, Scatter or Crystal Motor it touches by one Evolution, for twice the charge.
blockdesc-machine-motor-*: Awakened sparkstone carved into a hub. Its crystals, socketed on the glyph's face, turn the axle, gear or quern at the hub on the face opposite while the network pays. The stone stores no charge of its own; its aligned crystals store it.
itemdesc-crystalrod: Polished stone with an Unaligned crystal at its tip, Command's crystal. It switches Awakened stone, turns a machine's front and switches its crystals Dormant. It holds no charge and never wears out.
crystalrod-turn: Make this face the machine's front
crystalrod-rest: Switch the crystal looked at Dormant or awake
blockdesc-controlshelf-*: A stone shelf set with its back against a side of a Focus or Scatter. Its one to four items, left to right, are the machine's hands; the container at its left, as you face it, is the machine's input and the one at its right its output. Only Unaligned crystals work it.
controlshelf-asleep: The whole shelf is Dormant: an item is out of stock. It wakes when that stock arrives, or sneak and right-click it with the Crystal Rod.
controlshelf-prefix: (keeps the next tool to its kind)
blockdesc-memory-*: A module: Awakened sparkstone set against any face of a Focus or Scatter but its front. It holds a magazine of two crystals and, after each turn, swaps the crystal that just worked for the next one, for nothing.
blockdesc-reclamationplate: A thin copper plate laid under salt water. When a Fire Focus boils the water above it, the plate claims the salt, one time in four for each block boiled, into a container touching it.
itemdesc-deadsocket: A copper plug in a stone collar. Set into a Crystal Motor's socket, it turns the Motor straight from the line, as a small crystal would, for twice the charge. It stores nothing, and does nothing in any other socket.
machine-stoppedfull: Output full: Dormant until a rod tap.
journal-basicvocabulary-page1:
The Basic Vocabulary

Struck with the chisel, woken stone takes a verb. The face I strike becomes its front, carved with a glyph and four sockets: first Gather. Strike the front again for Refine, then Focus, Scatter, Amplify and the Crystal Motor, and once more for plain stone. It costs nothing and rings softly.

Stone with crystals in it will not take a new verb; I take them out first. Mined, a machine keeps its verb, and set down again it faces me.
journal-basicvocabulary-page2:
Every block of woken stone has room for four. A small crystal fills one socket and a Glowing one two, so a block holds four small ones, two Glowing ones, or one of each and a small one more. Right-click a crystal into the stone; take it back with an empty hand. Crouching still sets it standing on top.

In plain stone, and in a Crystal Motor, an aligned crystal is a capacitor: its room joins the line's and the line stores more. Taken out, it leaves as full as the line is.
journal-basicvocabulary-page3:
Every block of woken stone is Active or Dormant. A Dormant block's glyphs go dark: it passes no charge, so one cuts a line in two, and a Dormant machine does nothing at all.

The Crystal Rod switches them. I made mine by holding a block of polished rock against a placed Unaligned crystal for a breath; both went into it. Crouch and right-click stone to switch it. Right-click another face of a machine to turn its front there, crystals and all, and right-click a crystal on the front to switch it Dormant, its plug dark, or wake it. Each tap makes a machine look again at what touches it.
journal-basicvocabulary-page4: Gather drinks from where it stands. Each aligned crystal in it reads the same few blocks around as a standing crystal does and pours what it finds straight into the line: twice what a standing one takes in, three times that for a Glowing one, which wants a purer place. Fire by lava or a busy forge, Ice in snow and water, Earth deep in rock, Sky high in the open air.
journal-basicvocabulary-page5: Refine teaches. One aligned crystal in it is the pattern, and every Unaligned crystal beside it, no greater than the pattern, takes its alignment, wherever the block stands: a day for a small crystal, two for a Glowing one, paid from the line as it goes. Two patterns that disagree teach nothing.
journal-basicvocabulary-page6: Focus looks out of its front and works, every ten breaths for each crystal in turn, on what it sees, as far as a cast would reach: Fire lights, Ice quenches and waters tilled soil, Sky blows and gathers, and Earth raises a tower once and then sleeps until I tap it awake. A Glowing crystal works the square around what it sees. It costs a tenth of a cast, and nothing when there is nothing to do. What it gathers goes into a chest beside it.
journal-basicvocabulary-page7: Scatter trades strength for breadth: each crystal works one Evolution weaker, over a flat square nine blocks by nine. A small crystal has nothing to give up and does nothing there. Earth tills the soil instead of raising it, Ice waters it, and a Glowing Sky crystal with help reaps the whole field and sows it again from its own seed.
journal-basicvocabulary-page8:
Amplify lifts the Focus, Scatter or Motor it touches by one Evolution, for twice the charge, but only crystals no greater than its own. One is all a machine will take; a second beside it adds nothing. It does nothing for Gather or Refine.

The Crystal Motor keeps its glyph and sockets on the face I strike and its hub on the face behind, which turns the axle, gear or quern there, day and night, while the line pays: each small crystal as much as one length of windmill sails, a Glowing one three times as much. The Motor's own stone stores nothing; its aligned crystals store its charge, so cut off from the line it runs until they are spent, and an Unaligned crystal stores none. Tap it Dormant to stop it.
journal-basicvocabulary-page9:
Twins still quarrel in machines, so I keep them more than three blocks apart.

In a Focus each crystal works its own nature. Fire burns, Ice cools, Earth lifts, Sky moves. The Hidden Fifth has a nature too: it commands stone. And what is a cradle, if not carved stone?
journal-basicvocabulary-page10:
A Sky Focus aimed at a tree fells it whole, as an axe would, and the logs, sticks and saplings go to its output. It pays by the logs: a small crystal fells one log a working, a Glowing one nine, a Luminous one twenty-seven, and a tall tree takes several workings' charge at once.

An Earth Focus facing sideways or up bores: it takes a square two by two out of the rock in front of it, as deep as its crystal would raise a tower, and the ground goes into its output. It sleeps after each bore until I tap it awake.
journal-basicvocabulary-page11: Memory is a module, as Amplify is. A block of it, made from woken stone and a Glowing crystal, set against any face of a Focus or Scatter but its front, holds a magazine of two crystals. After each turn the crystal that just worked goes to the bottom of the magazine and the next one takes its place, so one socket works many natures in turn. A Dormant crystal in the magazine is passed over, and the swap costs nothing.
journal-basicvocabulary-page12:
The reclamation plate lies on the floor under salt water. When a Fire Focus boils the water above it, the plate claims the salt, one time in four for each block boiled, into a chest touching it. A hand cast claims nothing.

Goods travel in the game's own chutes and hoppers, and an Archimedes screw lifts them, turned by a Crystal Motor like any other power. A machine treats a chute or a hopper as a chest. When its output is full, a machine goes Dormant rather than spill, and waits for a rod tap once there is room.
journal-basicvocabulary-page13: The Dead Socket is a copper plug in a stone collar, set into a Crystal Motor's socket in place of a crystal. It turns the Motor straight from the line, as much as a small crystal, for twice its charge, and an Amplify doubles both. It stores nothing, so the Motor stops the moment its line is cut, empty or Dormant. In the socket on a Control Shelf's top it keeps the whole shelf to all or nothing. In any other socket it does nothing.
journal-controlshelf-page1:
The Control Shelf gives a Focus or Scatter hands. I set its back against a side of the machine, never the front, and lay up to four things on it. Only an Unaligned crystal works a shelf: each turn it does the first thing, left to right, that has work, so the order is the program.

The shelf is the machine's port too. Facing it, the chest at its left is the input and the chest at its right the output. What the shelf itself uses, firewood split while firewood is on the shelf, goes back to the input. Glyphs on its sides and front show which: points meeting for in, parting for out.
journal-controlshelf-page2:
What each thing on the shelf does in the reach, drawing what it needs from the input:

Seeds sow tilled soil. A sapling is planted on open ground. Fertiliser feeds farmland. A shovel digs soil, sand, gravel and charcoal. A bucket milks the animals ready for it into a barrel at the right. An axe splits logs into firewood. Firewood is stacked into piles and builds a firepit. A firestarter lights a charcoal pit or a cold firepit, never a pile and never a bomb.
journal-controlshelf-page3:
Something that names no work, set just left of a shovel or an axe, keeps that tool to its own kind. Charcoal before a shovel digs only finished charcoal, so the pit's stone walls stay; gravel digs only that gravel and sand only that sand. An oak log before an axe splits only oak, and only oak goes back to the input. Such a prefix is never used up and does nothing before anything else.

A prefix's plug follows its tool's.
journal-controlshelf-page4:
Under each place a plug in the ledge glows cyan while its thing is Active and goes dark when it is Dormant, whatever the reason. Right-click a thing with the Crystal Rod and it is switched off: the machine passes it over, as work and as stock, until another right-click wakes it. A prefix is never switched.

A thing also goes quiet by itself, its plug dark, and the machine stops looking at it. Out of stock, it wakes when its kind next comes into the input. Done, with nothing left to do in its reach, it stays quiet even when stock comes, until I wake it.
journal-controlshelf-page5:
Waking. Crouch and right-click the shelf with the rod, and it and every quiet thing wake together, but what I switched off stays off. A right-click wakes just one. Looking at the shelf tells me why each dark thing is dark: switched off, out of stock or done.

The shelf also has one socket in the middle of its top. With a Dead Socket in it, one thing out of stock sends the whole shelf Dormant, until that stock comes or I wake it.
journal-controlshelf-page6: Charcoal with no hand on it. The pit chars only when stone that does not burn closes in its piles and firepit, top included, and a chest or any wood touching them leaves them smouldering. A machine is stone and seals it as stone does. Firewood keeps the roofed cell straight in front of the machine for last and builds the firepit there, on the full pile beneath, and the firestarter lights it. A pit two layers high wants a machine that works both at once: a Glowing Unaligned crystal with an Amplify.
journal-controlshelf-page7:
Building the gate.
1. Dig a room into stone, three blocks deep, one wide and two high inside, under a stone roof.
2. In the middle of one end wall, level with the upper layer and facing in, set a Focus with a Glowing Unaligned crystal in it.
3. Set an Amplify against it in the wall, joined to my line.
4. Put the shelf on the Focus's back, outside the wall, with a chest of logs at its left and an empty chest at its right as I face it.
journal-controlshelf-page8:
5. Lay an axe, a shovel, firewood and a firestarter on the shelf, in that order.

It splits the logs, stacks the room with piles, keeping the cell in front of it for last, builds the firepit there and lights it. Each thing goes quiet as it is done, and the burn costs nothing.

6. After the pit's eighteen hours, crouch and right-click the shelf with the rod, once. The shovel digs the charcoal into the chest at the right and the next pit is stacked. One tap after each burn.
journal-quicken-page1:
Quicken

The first word of the Hidden Vocabulary. An Unaligned crystal in a Focus, aimed at a cradle where a seedling grows, hurries it on: each working brings as much growth as ten breaths would, a Glowing crystal twice that, so one small crystal doubles the growth and one Glowing crystal triples it. A Glowing Focus quickens every cradle in its square, and a Scatter every cradle in its field, one Evolution weaker.

Each working costs as any other, and only while a seedling grows.
